speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These amendments will strengthen Singapore's corporate governance regime and affirm our commitment to combating money laundering, terrorism financing and other threats to the integrity of the international financial system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The amendments will also bring us into closer alignment with the international standards set by the Financial Action Task Force, or FATF, of which Singapore is a member.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: FATF is an inter-governmental organisation that sets international standards to prevent global money laundering and terrorism financing and the harm that is caused to financial ecosystems and society at large.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MOF and the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) sought views from the public on the draft Bill in July last year and have taken in the feedback received where relevant and feasible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, the Companies Act already requires companies to maintain a Register of members or shareholders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In certain situations, a shareholder may hold shares on behalf of another person.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In such a situation, the person holding the shares is known as the nominee shareholder, while the person for whom the shares are held is known as the nominator.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our Acts today do not require the nominator to be identified, as he or she is not the shareholder on record.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, as the nominee shareholder typically acts on the instructions of the nominator, the lack of transparency on the identity of these persons who actually control the shares is an area of concern internationally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will ensure that nominators, who are effectively controllers of a company, are properly identified, in line with the international standards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With this amendment, nominee shareholders will also be required to inform the company of their nominee status and their nominators in a timely manner.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These amendments are provided for in clause 2(i) of the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The second set of amendments introduces new requirements in relation to the identification of registrable controllers, for local and foreign companies and LLPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, companies and LLPs are already required to maintain a Register of Registrable Controllers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These are individuals or corporate entities that have a significant interest in or significant control over the company or LLP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, there have been situations where a company or LLP claims to have no registrable controllers with significant interest or control.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Individuals with executive control are the chief executive officers (CEOs) and directors or partners who exercise executive control over the daily or regular affairs of the company or LLP through a senior management position.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will enhance the transparency of beneficial ownership and control of companies and LLPs in Singapore, by ensuring that a registrable controller is identified for all companies and LLPs, in line with international expectations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clauses 2(e) and 3(c) of the Bill provide for this amendment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Aside from these two sets of amendments, this Bill also seeks to clarify the timelines for local and foreign companies to update their various registers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Local companies are already required to maintain a Register of Nominee Directors, reflecting their status as a nominee director and the particulars of their nominator.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, no timeframe is specified for local companies to update their register when there is a change in particulars of the nominee director or their nominator.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Specifying a seven-day time limit for this provides clarity on the expected timeline and will ensure that the register is updated in a timely manner.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clause 2(f) of the Bill provides for this amendment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Foreign companies are already required to keep a Register of Members at their Singapore branch, but, currently, there is no timeframe specified as to when updates must be made when there is a change in their members' particulars.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This amendment will, similarly, provide clarity to the foreign companies on the timeline expected for updating their register.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have allowed a longer timeframe for foreign companies to give them sufficient time to contact their members who may be based overseas and to update their register.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clause 2(a) of the Bill provides for this amendment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The proposed amendments in this Bill on the new registers to be maintained and the clarification of the timelines within which the various registers must be updated will strengthen Singapore's regime on the transparency and beneficial ownership of companies and LLPs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Preventing the illicit movement of funds is key to Singapore's role as a respected international financial hub and I am glad we are taking steps to strengthen our protections.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Does this mean that no other person can have executive control and is not relevant to be disclosed in the register?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, this requirement seems repetitive, given that the information about directors and CEOs are already filed with ACRA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What would be necessary before someone is considered "accustomed"?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The amendment states that the nominee must also receive dividends on behalf of the principal shareholder.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is it sufficient that there is an agreement for the nominee to receive dividends, or must there be an actual distribution into the hands of the nominee?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If it is the latter, this creates a problem where it is impossible to clarify nominee status for companies that do not issue dividends.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new regulations apply not only to multinational corporations or financial institutions but also small local businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For small businesses, these rules can be complex and require proportionally larger costs to comply with.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How will the Ministry support our small businesses to ensure these regulations do not unfairly burden them?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In summary, I seek clarification on three things: the need to list directors or CEOs in the register, the definition of nominee shareholders and the ways the Ministry will support small businesses in complying with the new regulations.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The proposed amendments are a result of recommendations made by the inter-governmental body, known as the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: These amendments concern administrative requirements applicable to companies in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My speech will support the Bill but raise questions and suggestions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The Singapore Government's stated aims have been to detect, deter and prevent money laundering and terrorism financing and to protect the integrity of its financial system from illegal activities and elicit fund flows.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Singapore has continued, I note, to make progress to address the technical compliance deficiencies identified in the latest 2019 FATF Mutual Evaluation Report, or MER.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: As a result of this progress, Singapore has been re-rated on several Recommendations, that is, Nos 3, 23, 24 and 25.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Take, for instance, the amendment of the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act, which came into effect in April 2019.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The increase in fines through these Acts were considered sufficiently dissuasive in the said MER, which led Singapore to be re-rated as compliant with Recommendation 3, bringing Singapore closer to its goal of deterring money laundering and terrorist financing activities.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, Singapore has not addressed all the identified deficiencies and several areas for improvement still exist.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In order to strengthen Singapore's measures to fight money laundering and terrorism financing, the Corporate Registers (Amendment) Bill is necessary to keep Singapore's legal regime aligned with FATF's standards and recommendations.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The first point concerns the different timelines for local and foreign companies in updating their registers of key personnel.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The Bill originally intended that foreign companies should update the register of members within 14 days.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, during the public consultation phase, the feedback was that this would be a challenge for foreign companies, especially if they have more than 50 members.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: While the feedback suggested that companies should be given 14 to 28 days, MOF and ACRA further extended the deadline to 30 days, stating that this would be aligned with the requirements in section 372 of the Companies Act.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In other words, this feedback was accepted in the spirit of harmonising timelines in existing legal provisions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, this is a commendable, reasonable and consistent approach that avoids imposing multiple timelines and requirements on foreign companies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, feedback to amend requirements for local companies for consistency with existing legislation was not received in the same way.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The amendment Bill, currently, intends for local companies to update their information on nominee directors and shareholders within seven days.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The implication is that local companies now have two timelines to follow: seven days to update particulars for nominee, directors; and 14 days for particulars of all other key personnel.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This begs the following question: what is the basis for requiring that local companies must update their information and nominee directors within a seven-day period when there is already an existing requirement to update information on various key position holders within 14 days?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The hon Minister Indranee Rajah stated earlier in her Second Reading speech that foreign companies may need more time to contact overseas stakeholders, directors, but local companies may also have some directors residing overseas, either on a long-term basis or who may be overseas at the relevant time.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, I am wondering why the timelines for both local and foreign companies cannot be harmonised.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Singapore has made great progress in implementing Recommendation 24 on Transparency and Beneficial Ownership of Legal Persons through an amendment to the Companies Act in 2017 and further amendments in this Corporate Registers Bill before us.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Singapore has strengthened its compliance with Recommendation 24 where Singapore was rated as "largely compliant".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, Sir, the remaining other FATF recommendations which Singapore was found to be only "partially compliant with" are Recommendations 22, 28 and 35.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Recommendation 22 concerns the application of customer due diligence and record-keeping requirements to designated non-financial businesses and professions (DNFBPs), such as the gambling and legal Industries.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Recommendation 28 is about subjecting the aforementioned DNFBPs to regulatory and supervisory framework regarding anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing measures.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Recommendation 35 relates to the available range of sanctions to do with parties that have failed to abide by anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing measures.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: These terms include "individuals with executive control", "executive control", and "accustomed".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I ask this, considering the need to avoid business uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Can such guidance be expected shortly upon the Bill's passage or coming into force?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Louis Ng raised three points of clarification, which I will address in turn.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, Mr Louis Ng asked about the rationale for identifying CEOs and directors with executive control to be listed in the Register of Registrable Controllers, if a company is unable to identify a registrable controller.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As I had explained in my speech earlier, there have been situations where a company claimed to have no registrable controllers with significant interest or control.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Currently, such companies would not be required to enter any particulars into the register of controllers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The intent of the Register of Registrable Controllers is to increase the transparency of natural persons who have beneficial ownership and control of companies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is, therefore, necessary to include these persons in the Register if no other controller can be identified.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked if it is necessary to provide particulars of the CEO and the directors in the register of registrable controllers when ACRA may already have the information in other registers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The reality is that a company can have many directors, but not all of them exercise executive control over the company.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The purpose of the new requirement is to ensure that companies identify the directors and CEOs with executive control, so that the beneficial owners are properly identified.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Next, let me address Mr Louis Ng's clarification on the definition of a nominee shareholder.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: A shareholder is considered to be a nominee if he fulfils the following two criteria in respect of the shares that he holds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, he is accustomed to, or under an obligation, to vote in accordance with the instructions of any other person.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The word "accustomed" suggests some degree of habit – meaning that there must be some consistent pattern of behaviour of the nominee shareholder voting in accordance with the instructions or wishes of any other person – and occasional instances of such behaviour would not be sufficient to constitute "accustomed".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second criterion is that he or she receives dividends on behalf of his or her nominator.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Lastly, Mr Louis Ng asked about the compliance cost of the new requirements and the support that Government will put in place.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To be clear and, as mentioned in my speech earlier, out of the four sets of amendments in this Bill, two are clarifications on timelines and only two are new requirements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The new requirement to maintain a Register of Nominee Shareholders is unlikely to materially increase compliance costs, especially if the small businesses do not have nominee arrangements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Moreover, the responsibility on the company is only to maintain such a register, based on declarations by nominee shareholders.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Companies will not be required to send notices to check if shareholders are nominees.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The other new requirement is to identify individuals with the executive control of a company or LLP to be listed in the Register of Registrable Controllers, if they are unable to identify a registrable controller.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Small businesses that are set up as sole proprietorships or general partnerships will not be impacted by them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government will help companies and LLPs to comply with the new requirements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: ACRA will issue a Guidance on the new requirement of maintaining a Register of Nominee Shareholders.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Guidance will contain detailed instructions to clarify and explain the new requirements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, it will provide details on how a nominee shareholder and nominator can be identified and include a model template to support the maintenance of the register.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: ACRA will also update the existing Guidance on the Register of Registrable Controllers for companies and LLPs to provide clarity on how these entities can identify persons with executive control as registrable controllers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Leon Perera had a number of questions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The first one, I believe, relates to the different timeframes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The 30-day timeframe for foreign companies to update the Register of members is consistent with section 372 of the Companies Act, which requires foreign companies to update any changes in their particulars in ACRA's registers within 30 days.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This also provides sufficient time for foreign companies to contact members who are located overseas and update the Register which is located in the registered office in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In comparison, local companies are to update the Register of Nominee Directors within seven days of being informed of any changes by the nominee director.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This provides sufficient time for local companies to update the register whilst ensuring that the registers are updated in a timely manner.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The general principle, really, is of the underlying assumption that if it is a local director, then it will be easier to contact the relevant persons and to do the updating.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is not something which is particularly unique or startling, for the simple reason that there are many types of deadlines where more time is given to foreign companies, simply because they need to contact people who are overseas.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second item that he raised was about items where we are partially compliant, rather than fully compliant.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That will be done as soon as reasonably practicable.
